notes:
- The trailer window closes as one picture: The scrim and the chrome faded on the way out, but the video did not: a WebView is a real View and no Compose layer can fade one, so the player sat at full strength inside a window that was pretending to be gone until the dialog was torn down. It fades with everything else now, on the same clock, and it also cannot appear before its frame has arrived. The platform's own hard dim behind the dialog is gone for the same reason - it cut to black on the frame the viewer opened and back again on the way out, over a scrim that was already animating - and the player finally hides the system bars and stays clear of a camera hole.
- The loading ring hands over instead of blinking out: The ring was removed in the frame the embed reported in, one frame before the player had any alpha of its own, so a black box appeared between the spinner and the video. The two crossfade now, and the ring keeps turning through its own fade rather than vanishing one frame into it.
- Notifications arrive once: A new row was faded in twice - by its own entrance and by the list item - so it arrived at the square of the curve its neighbours were on, visibly slower than the cards above it. The list only moves rows now, and the movement comes from the app's motion tokens, so a reader who asked for Instant motion no longer gets rows sliding into place.
- The trailer plays inside the app: The Nova page's trailer card and the Extras row now open a player over the page instead of handing the video to a browser: the thumbnail stays as its backdrop, the title travels with it, and Open on YouTube remains as the escape hatch for a region lock or an age gate. A trailer whose AniList id is missing still opens externally, because there is nothing to embed.
- The loading ring is wavy again: The circle that spins behind a starting trailer was drawn the whole time and was never visible: the WebView is a real View, and Views paint above everything Compose draws, so an opaque black one covered the ring until the embed's first paint - and that first paint fired at the wrong moment anyway. The player now starts transparent and fades in on the page's own signal that the frame has loaded, with a timeout so a player that never loads cannot leave the ring spinning forever.
- Pulling the title sheet down no longer stops responding: The drag fraction the sheet's settle reads was captured once by the gesture, so every further frame compared a number from the first frame of the pull and the sheet could stick halfway. The gesture reads the live value now, and the settle still snaps to the same three stops.
- Zooming the artwork is animated: A double-tap used to jump the picture to 2.4x with no frame in between, which reads as the image being replaced rather than enlarged. It travels on the app's settling spring, and a pinch cancels it - so the two gestures cannot fight over the scale.
- The fill does not replay when you change its style: The bar's once-per-title entrance flag lived inside the drawing, and choosing a style replaced the drawing - the new one filled from zero under the finger that had just picked it over a progress that had not changed. The flag belongs to the card now and survives the switch.
- The Info page counts its score in: The score chip's number travels up to its value on the same spring the sections arrive on, once per title, instead of appearing at full value with the page. Numbers AniList did not send are still left out rather than counted to zero.
- Tiles cast the same shadow on every phone: The dragged tier tile and its tray ghost asked for a shadow in pixels while naming it in dp, so the same lift was a 6dp shadow on one screen and 8dp on another. Both ask in dp now.
- The planning button stopped rebuilding sixty times a second: Holding Add to Planning animated its colour, its corner radius and its fill from a value read while composing, so a three-second hold recomposed the whole control - label swap, confirm squares and gesture chain - on every frame. Those three reads happen while drawing now; the hold animates exactly as before, and costs a repaint.
